matter: fx-flathub-detect.sh — a bash library for detecting whether the Flathub remote is enabled in a Flatpak installation, with multi-scope (system/user) detection, lazy caching, and config file fallback.
claims: The library correctly uses type -P for flatpak binary lookup, avoiding alias/function resolution
The detection ladder (binary → remote-list → config fallback) is architecturally sound
Scope semantics (system|user|both|empty) correctly represent where Flathub is enabled
The command path via flatpak remote-list is distro-agnostic and authoritative
Config file fallback only triggers when binary is absent or all remote-list calls fail
The config parser correctly handles case-insensitive enabled=false values
Binary validation via allowlist prevents PATH injection attacks
TOCTOU mitigation with dual validation (original + canonical) eliminates symlink races
Lazy caching via _FLATHUB_DETECTED flag runs detection at most once per shell
Cache integrity verification with content hashes detects external state drift
All globals are always written, making the library safe for set -u callers
Double-source guard prevents re-initialization side effects
Direct execution guard correctly exits with code 2 and usage hint
Debug redaction covers major sensitive path patterns (home, nix store, homebrew)
State machine correctly prioritizes ENABLED over UNKNOWN when flathub found in any scope
Configured-but-disabled detection via --show-disabled works correctly per scope
Scope normalization handles space-joined lists and maps to stable vocabulary
flathub_enabled predicate correctly returns 0 iff enabled, safe for if guards
flathub_state echoes correct enum: enabled|disabled|not-configured|unknown|flatpak-missing
flathub_scope echoes correct enum: system|user|both|empty
Binary allowlist covers all common distro paths including NixOS and Homebrew
Config path allowlist correctly validates freedesktop-standard paths
Source guard return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0 handles non-standard sourcing contexts
flathub_scope_enabled correctly distinguishes not-enabled from error conditions
